# Claude Code Settings

Settings are JSON files that change how Claude Code behaves.
You can pick a model, add permission rules, turn off a feature, or share the same rules with a whole team.
For example, a `.claude/settings.json` file with `{ "model": "opus" }` makes each session in that project start on Opus.

## Marks

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ | A page of the [Claude Code docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) names it. |
| 🔍 | Only the Claude Code bundle names it. No docs page does. |
| ⚠️ | The docs and the bundle differ. The row says how. |
| 🧪 | It works only behind a flag, a plan, or a server-side switch. The row says which. |
| ❌ | It is removed or does nothing in `2.1.303`. |

A `-` in the `Default` column means that neither the docs nor the schema state a default.
The `Scope` column says which settings files may set the key.
`Any file` means the user, project, local, and managed files.

## Pages for Each Group of Keys

The managed schema of `2.1.303` lists 184 keys.
The user schema lists 162, and the other 22 are managed-only.
Each key has a row on one of these pages.

| Page | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| [Core](Claude-Code-Settings-Core) | Compaction, memory, cleanup, shell, files, `env`, `sandbox`, updates |
| [Model](Claude-Code-Settings-Model) | Model, effort, thinking, fast mode, cache lifetime, token reminders |
| [Auth](Claude-Code-Settings-Auth) | Credential helpers, login rules, API provider limits |
| [Agents and Remote](Claude-Code-Settings-Agents-And-Remote) | `agent`, workflows, background work, Remote Control, peer sessions |
| [Hooks and Plugins](Claude-Code-Settings-Hooks-And-Plugins) | Hooks, plugins, marketplaces, skills, `permissions`, `statusLine`, `outputStyle` |
| [MCP and Channels](Claude-Code-Settings-MCP-And-Channels) | MCP servers, claude.ai connectors, channels |
| [UI](Claude-Code-Settings-UI) | Theme, spinner, `tui`, voice, notices, feedback |
| [Enterprise](Claude-Code-Settings-Enterprise) | How managed policy arrives, version limits |
| [Extra Keys](Claude-Code-Settings-Extra-Keys) | Keys that the schema omits, and the keys of `~/.claude.json` |

## Where Settings Live

| Scope | File | Who it affects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User | `~/.claude/settings.json` | You, in every project. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` moves `~/.claude`. |
| Shared project | `.claude/settings.json` | Everyone who works in the folder. Commit it so teammates get it. |
| Project local | `.claude/settings.local.json` | You, in this project only. Claude Code keeps the file out of git. |
| Command line | `--settings <file-or-json>` | One session. It cannot set `Managed` or `Global config` keys. |
| Managed | `managed-settings.json` and the other managed sources | Everyone your organization deploys it to. |
| Global config | `~/.claude.json` | You. Claude Code writes it. It holds sign-in data, MCP servers, per-project state, and a few keys. |

Source: [Settings Files and Precedence](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings) and [Explore the .claude Directory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory).

- Settings files are strict JSON.
  A comment or a trailing comma is a syntax error.
- Claude Code reads the shared project file from the primary working directory.
  After `/cd`, it reads the new directory (v2.1.246 or later).
- In a git repository, the local file lives at the repository root.
  In a worktree, it lives at the main checkout root.
- Claude Code adds `**/.claude/settings.local.json` to your global git excludes file when it writes the local file.
- Claude Code watches the files and reloads them.
  It runs the `ConfigChange` hook for each change in a settings file.
- Managed settings from MDM or the console reach a running session on a schedule, not on save.
- A cloud session reads only the shared project file and server-managed settings.
- Run `/status` to see the `Setting sources` line.
  Run `claude doctor` to see the entries that Claude Code dropped.
- The flag `--setting-sources <sources>` loads only the sources you name (`user`, `project`, `local`).

The bundle names the five sources `userSettings`, `projectSettings`, `localSettings`, `flagSettings`, and `policySettings`.

## Which Value Wins

The highest level that sets a key wins.

1. Managed settings.
2. Command line (`--settings`).
3. Project local settings.
4. Shared project settings.
5. User settings.

Environment variables are not a level.
Each pair of key and variable decides alone, such as `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` over `model`.
See [Env Vars](Claude-Code-Env-Vars).
Source: [Settings Files and Precedence](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings).

## How Lists and Model Keys Merge

- List keys such as `permissions.allow` merge across scopes.
- `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` stops that merge for permission rules.
- `fallbackModel` is an ordered chain.
  The whole value comes from the highest scope that sets it.
- `modelPicker` never merges.
  The whole value comes from managed settings, `--settings`, or user settings.
  Claude Code ignores project and local values (v2.1.242 or later).
- `availableModels`: a managed list applies as it is.
  Across the other scopes, the arrays merge.
- `modelSettings` resolves one model at a time, together with `effortLevel`.
- Managed `env` blocks merge per key across admin sources.
  `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADMIN_ENV_UNION=1` turns that off ([Environment Variables](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars)).

## Managed Settings

An administrator puts managed settings on a machine in one of these ways.
Source: [Deploy Managed Settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings).

| Platform | Where Claude Code looks |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json`, and the `com.anthropic.claudecode` managed preferences domain |
| Linux and WSL | `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json` |
| Windows | `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json`, and the registry keys `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode` and `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode` |
| WSL on Windows | The Windows sources, only when `wslInheritsWindowsSettings` is on |
| All | The `managed-settings.d/` folder next to the file, server-managed settings (cached in `~/.claude/remote-settings.json`), and the SDK `managedSettings` option or `--managed-settings` flag |

- Claude Code merges `managed-settings.json` first, then each `*.json` file of `managed-settings.d/` in alphabetical order.
  Number the files to set the order, such as `10-telemetry.json`.
- `managedSourcesBehavior` decides how sources combine.
  `first-wins` uses the highest source alone.
  `merge` deep-merges them.
- `parentSettingsBehavior` does the same for the SDK parent tier.
- `policyHelper` and `policyHelpers` compute managed settings at startup.

## Exceptions to Managed Precedence

For a few keys, a lower scope may set a stricter value, and Claude Code honors it over the managed value.
Source: [Settings Files and Precedence](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings).

| Mark | Key | Value Claude Code honors | Where from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✅ | `disableClaudeAiConnectors`, `isolatePeerMachines`, `permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` | `true` | Any scope |
| ✅ | `enableArtifact`, `disableArtifact` | `enableArtifact: false` or `disableArtifact: true` | Any scope |
| ✅ | `autoMode.classifyAllShell` | `true` | `~/.claude/settings.json` or `--settings` |
| ✅ | `remoteControlAtStartup` | `false` | `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json` |
| ✅ | `crossSessionInbound` | A stricter value on the ladder `accept`, `hold`, `refuse` | `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json` |
| ✅ | `useAutoModeDuringPlan`, `syncClaudeAiSkills`, `syncClaudeAiPlugins` | `false` | Managed, `--settings`, `~/.claude/settings.json`, or `.claude/settings.local.json` |
| ✅ | `maxEffortLevel` | The lowest cap (v2.1.267 or later) | Any scope |
| 🔍 | `modelProposedGoals`, `feedbackDrafts`, `availableModelsMatch`, `askUserQuestionTimeout`, `dialogExpiry` | A strict value | The bundle lists them as keys with a strict value. The docs do not list them here. |

An app that runs Claude Code inside itself and sets `CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST` is also an exception.
Claude Code then takes the model keys of that app over the managed values.
